observed_synopsis: Philadelphia Presbytery ordered Christ Church, Oreland’s Session to transfer three ruling elders while their judicial cases were on appeal. The General Assembly adopted its special Judicial Commission’s judgment rejecting the improper-debate specification for insufficient documentation but sustaining the constitutional challenge: BCO 12-5 and the separation of church-court powers reserve membership control to the Session, which correctly withheld transfer during pending judicial process. The judgment annulled Presbytery’s instruction and imposed three-year constitutional-inquiry safeguards, plus Digest purchase and officer review.

raw_title: TE John T. DeBardeleben v. Philadelphia Presbytery
parties: TE John T. DeBardeleben; Philadelphia Presbytery
observed_synopsis: A complaint challenged Philadelphia Presbytery’s approval of proceedings that cleared teaching and ruling elders without properly trying serious public accusations arising from Christ Church’s division. All three specifications were sustained because plea bargaining, dropped charges, and failure to hear necessary witnesses left the accusations unresolved. Presbytery’s action was annulled and de novo trials produced mixed convictions and acquittals. Harold Burkhart received six months’ suspension, Douglas McCready an admonition, and six former ruling elders three-month suspensions. The decision stressed taking such conflicts to Presbytery or judicial process rather than the congregation.

observed_synopsis: The CJB found the complaint of the Session of First PCA, Rowlett, TX against North Texas Presbytery to be in order and recommended that a commission be appointed to adjudicate the case. No substantive details of the complaint are provided.

The complaint challenged Philadelphia Presbytery's debate and instruction that Christ Church, Oreland transfer three members. The commission did not sustain the debate specification but held that Presbytery lacked constitutional authority to command the transfers, sustained that specification, and annulled the instruction by an 18-0 vote.

Complainants challenged Philadelphia Presbytery's disposition of indictments arising from the division of Christ Reformed Presbyterian Church, Oreland. The commission sustained the principal specifications, annulled Presbytery's adoption of its judicial commission report, tried the matters de novo, and imposed censures on ministers and former ruling elders.

The complaint challenged Philadelphia Presbytery's reception of a complaint that had not first been filed with the primary court, its judgment of members without process, and its attempt to act for a Session. The commission sustained the errors, annulled the March 12, 1988 actions, and directed corrective action by an 18-0 vote.

observed_synopsis: TE Vaughn Hathaway complained that the Session of Waynesboro Presbyterian Church refused to furnish him, as pastor and member of the Session, with copies of financial reports the Session had authorized. The panel found Specification 6 sustained (the pastor had a right to the reports as a session member) but declared the complaint moot because Hathaway's pastoral relation had been terminated before the case was decided.

raw_title: Grace Covenant Presbyterian Church v. New River Presbytery
parties: Grace Covenant Presbyterian Church, Blacksburg, VA; New River Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Grace Covenant Presbyterian Church complained against New River Presbytery's action sustaining a complaint that a Sunday school teacher holding theistic evolution and other doctrinal exceptions should not teach. The SJC partially sustained the complaint, declining to refer the matter back to the church with instructions but advising that the teacher should not teach while he holds exceptions that could require him to teach contrary to the fundamentals of the system of doctrine.

parties: R.E. Charles E. Chappell; Eastern Carolina Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Ruling Elder Chappell complained against Eastern Carolina Presbytery's Commission, which had suspended the session of Fuller Memorial Presbyterian Church and constituted itself as a 'Session Pro Tem' without due process or congregational consent. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that the BCO grants no authority for a presbytery to depose a session and act in its place, that suspension requires due process, and that the congregation has an inalienable right to be governed by officers it has chosen.

parties: T.E. Wallace W. Marshall, Jr.; Eastern Carolina Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Teaching Elder Wallace Marshall complained against the same Eastern Carolina Presbytery actions at Fuller Memorial Presbyterian Church that were the subject of Case 90-4, filed separately as a Teaching Elder complainant. The SJC sustained this complaint on essentially the same grounds as Case 90-4, finding that the presbytery lacked authority to suspend the session without due process and to constitute itself as a 'Session Pro Tem.'

raw_title: Melton et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
parties: Bryan Melton, Mrs. Bryan Melton, and Mrs. JoAnn Davis; Tennessee Valley Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Complainants challenged the ruling of the session of Westminster Presbyterian Church (Chattanooga) disallowing proxy votes at a December 10, 1989 congregational meeting that voted not to rescind the earlier dissolution and property transfer to New City Fellowship. The SJC denied all specifications, holding that proxy voting was not required under BCO 24-4 or Robert's Rules, and that the congregation's decision to dissolve was within its rights under BCO Chapter 25.

parties: Randy C. Stringer; Mississippi Valley Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Randy Stringer appealed his excommunication by Mississippi Valley Presbytery after being deposed and then excommunicated for failure to respond to the presbytery. The SJC set aside the excommunication and remanded the case to MVP, holding that after deposition the presbytery was required under BCO 46-8 to assign Stringer to membership in a particular church rather than proceed to excommunication. Dr. Morton H. Smith dissented, arguing that the presbytery had proper grounds to proceed to excommunication after Stringer's contumacy.

parties: T.E. David E. Bowen; Eastern Carolina Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE David Bowen complained against Eastern Carolina Presbytery's actions rescinding its 1988 decision and annulling the elections and ordinations of ruling elders and deacons at the Church of the Good Shepherd who took exception to infant baptism and limited atonement. The SJC sustained the complaint that ECP erred in rescinding a two-year-old action and annulling ordinations without due process under BCO 24-6, while also affirming that infant baptism and limited atonement are fundamentals of the system of doctrine for which no exceptions may be granted for church officers.

parties: Vaughn E. Hathaway, Jr. (TE); Grace Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Vaughn Hathaway complained that the Session of Waynesboro Presbyterian Church failed to institute discipline against seven members who had not attended worship for over a year. The judicial panel denied the complaint on the grounds that the Session retained discretion to determine the timing of discipline proceedings, and procedural errors did not result in material prejudice.

Sandra Lovelace submitted two letters challenging actions of Northeast Presbytery. The SJC found both administratively and judicially out of order because the first had not been presented first to the lower court and the second lacked supporting reasons and identified no complainable presbytery action under BCO 43-2 and 43-3.

raw_title: Nickoley and Stephens v. Southwest Presbytery
parties: Bruce Nickoley and David Stephens; Southwest Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Bruce Nickoley and David Stephens complained against Southwest Presbytery's actions in withdrawing charges against two ruling elders, dissolving a pastoral relationship, and rescinding its suspension of a local church session. The SJC denied the complaint, affirming that the Presbytery correctly determined it lacked constitutional authority to suspend the session or act as a 'Session pro tem' without congregational consent, and that original jurisdiction over charges against ruling elders rested with the local session.

parties: Mrs. Sandra Lovelace; Northeast Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Mrs. Sandra Lovelace complained against Northeast Presbytery's decision not to proceed to trial against teaching and ruling elders, and its ruling that her subsequent complaints were out of order due to non-membership. The SJC (reversing the Judicial Panel) denied the first item but sustained the second, holding that jurisdiction properly invoked is not forfeited by a subsequent change in the complainant's membership status.

parties: Frank J. Smith; Northeast Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Frank J. Smith complained against Northeast Presbytery after Grace Presbyterian Church was dissolved and its members were placed under Presbytery's care. The SJC ruled the complaint in order, sustained it, and returned the matter to Presbytery for adjudication, holding that dissolution did not eliminate Presbytery's pastoral responsibility or Smith's standing in the pending case.

parties: Virgil B. Roberts; New River Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Virgil B. Roberts complained that New River Presbytery delayed dissolving his pastoral relationship after he resigned and the congregation concurred. The SJC sustained the complaint, concluding that Presbytery should have acted on the agreed request rather than withholding dissolution; three commissioners dissented concerning Presbytery's constitutional authority and pastoral discretion.

Central Carolina Presbytery referred several interconnected complaints and disciplinary matters involving Prosperity Presbyterian Church to the SJC. Because still other related complaints had not been referred and the intended scope of the reference was unclear, the SJC declined adjudication and returned all the referred matters to Presbytery; deciding only the selected matters could have made the others moot without due consideration.

raw_title: Antioch Session v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery
parties: Antioch Session; Eastern Carolina Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Antioch Session complained that Eastern Carolina Presbytery erred in licensing Arthur Peterson given his divorce/remarriage history and his views on creation and a local flood. The SJC did not sustain the complaint on Issue 1 (licensure approval, 13-4), finding ECP acted with constitutional thoroughness and that precedent permitted a divorced man to hold office under certain conditions, but did sustain Issue 2 (3-0 panel; 17-0 SJC), finding ECP negligent in allowing Peterson to serve as stated supply for over six months before licensing him.

parties: Frank J. Smith; Northeast Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Frank J. Smith challenged Northeast Presbytery's actions surrounding the dissolution of Grace Presbyterian Church and the administration of its former members. The SJC denied the complaint by a 20-2 vote, with a dissent disputing the majority's treatment of the complainant's constitutional and procedural claims.

parties: Edgar Davis Johnson; Evangel Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Edgar Davis Johnson appealed Evangel Presbytery's judgment in a disciplinary case arising from his pursuit of divorce on a claim of spiritual desertion. The SJC did not sustain the appeal, approving the proposed decision by a 21-1 vote.

observed_synopsis: Case 2002-03 was decided with Cases 2001-34 and 2002-02. The SJC ruled some constituent complaints out of order but sustained the central complaint that James River Presbytery unduly delayed acting on a congregation's proper request to dissolve its pastoral relationship; it denied a related complaint concerning a salary gift. The consolidated decision drew concurring and dissenting opinions.

Dr. and Mrs. Frank Chin v. Covenant Presbytery
Westminster Presbyterian Church v. Westminster Presbytery

observed_synopsis: TE Stuart Merriam appealed against Tennessee Valley Presbytery, but withdrew Case 2004-10 before the SJC issued a merits decision.

Tim J. Harris v. Heritage Presbytery
APPEAL OF TE AURELIANO TAN, JR. VS. HOUSTON METRO PRESBYTERY

parties: RE Leland Nichols and RE Sam Couch; James River Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Three combined judicial cases (2001-34, 2002-02, 2002-03) arising from West End Presbyterian Church's attempts to dissolve its pastoral relationship with TE Robert Wilson; James River Presbytery repeatedly delayed or refused to grant the congregation's constitutionally-made request. The SJC sustained the complaints (13-3), holding that JRP had no constitutional basis to delay granting the congregation's properly voted request to dissolve the pastoral relationship, though several of the 17 individual complaints were ruled judicially out of order.

parties: TE James Thornton; Westminster Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE James Thornton complained that Westminster Presbytery erred by declining to place a valid call from Memorial PCA into his hands and simultaneously invoking BCO 34-10 to begin divestiture proceedings. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that the administrative remedy of BCO 34-10 cannot be invoked when a call is already in the presbytery's possession, and that presbytery's refusal lacked objective, justifiable grounds required for appellate review.

parties: TE Michael Chastain; Heritage Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Michael Chastain appealed his conviction and indefinite suspension by Heritage Presbytery for divisive behavior, arising from his public letters to his congregation disagreeing with Session actions regarding an associate pastor call and a related Christian school controversy. The SJC denied the appeal (20-1), upholding the conviction and censure while finding procedural errors that did not rise to reversible level; a dissent by RE Frederick Neikirk argued the charge of 'divisive behavior' failed BCO 29-1's requirement that offenses be proven from Scripture.

raw_title: Session of Hudson Korean American Presbyterian Church v. Korean Eastern Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found the Session of Hudson Korean American Presbyterian Church's complaint against Korean Eastern Presbytery out of order. The published Assembly report gives no reason and contains no merits opinion.

raw_title: Witcher Memorial re: 2004-05 Blevins v. Westminster Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found the Witcher Memorial concerning Case 2004-05, Blevins v. Westminster Presbytery, in order, but its officers determined not to hear it. The published Assembly report supplies no further reason or merits ruling.

parties: TE Peter B. Kim; Korean Eastern Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Peter B. Kim appealed his deposition and excommunication by Korean Eastern Presbytery on charges of contumacy and threatening members with civil litigation. The SJC sustained the contumacy charge and deposition but reduced the excommunication to indefinite suspension from the sacraments as excessive; it declined to rule on the civil-threat charge because the relevant letter was not in the Record of the Case.

parties: TE Peter B. Kim; Korean Eastern Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Peter B. Kim complained that Korean Eastern Presbytery erred in denying his complaint regarding unconstitutional actions of KEP's Administrative Commission, which had unlawfully exercised judicial powers in ordering a congregational meeting and dissolving his pastoral relationship. The SJC agreed KEP erred but held the matter moot in light of Kim's deposition in Case 2005-8, with a dissent arguing the constitutional violations by KEP were serious and should have been remedied.

raw_title: Memorial from Central Carolina Presbytery re: Louisiana Presbytery and TE J. Steven Wilkins
parties: Central Carolina Presbytery (Memorial); Louisiana Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Central Carolina Presbytery sent a memorial alleging that TE J. Steven Wilkins of Louisiana Presbytery was teaching doctrines (Federal Vision/Auburn Avenue theology) in flagrant contradiction to the Westminster Standards regarding election, covenant, and baptism. The SJC, after extended proceedings and directing Louisiana Presbytery to re-examine TE Wilkins, found Louisiana Presbytery had not adequately addressed the concerns and directed it via amends to appear under BCO 40-5 to account for its actions.

raw_title: Complaint of TE Eliot Lee vs. Korean Eastern Presbytery
Complaint of RE S. Han vs. Korean Eastern Presbytery
complaint. Case 2005-11, Hugo Andrino v. Southern Florida Presbytery

parties: TE Eliot Lee; Korean Eastern Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC sustained TE Eliot Lee's complaint against KEP for filing a civil lawsuit in New Jersey state court to adjudicate ecclesiastical matters (i.e., who was the rightful pastor of HKPC). The opinion affirms that PCA church courts have no authority to use civil courts to enforce ecclesiastical decisions, and that the PCA is a non-hierarchical denomination whose authority is moral and spiritual, not civil or coercive.

raw_title: David Kniseley et al. v. Rocky Mountain Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE David Kniseley and others challenged Rocky Mountain Presbytery's approval of the public title ‘Minister of Church Life’ for an unordained female staff member. The SJC denied the complaint, distinguishing the BCO's technical use of minister from generic staff titles and leaving the latter to lower-court judgment; a dissent disagreed.

parties: TE Eliot Lee; Korean Eastern Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC sustained two consolidated complaints by TE Eliot Lee against Korean Eastern Presbytery, annulling KEP's actions in empowering a Pulpit (Stated Supply Approval) Commission to act on behalf of the HKPC session without congregational consent, and annulling KEP's filing of a civil lawsuit in New Jersey state court to adjudicate ecclesiastical matters. The opinion extensively discusses the non-hierarchical nature of PCA polity and the limits of a presbytery's authority over local congregations.

raw_title: Session of Crossroads Community Church v. Philadelphia Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The Session of Crossroads Community Church challenged Philadelphia Presbytery's licensing and ordination of a candidate who stated a difference concerning women and the office of deacon but agreed to follow the BCO. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed Presbytery's judgment; a dissent argued it should have been sustained.

raw_title: Mark Grasso et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery
observed_synopsis: RE Mark Grasso and others challenged Philadelphia Presbytery's licensure and ordination of Jason Hsu, who held a stated difference concerning women deacons but affirmed willingness to follow the BCO. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed Presbytery's actions; a dissent was recorded.

raw_title: Broadwater et al. v. Chesapeake Presbytery
parties: TE Daniel Broadwater et al.; Chesapeake Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Chesapeake Presbytery appointed a commission to assume original jurisdiction over Grace Reformed Presbyterian Church of Relay, MD, without first making a finding that the Session had refused to act in a case of process. The SJC vacated the portion of the commission's mandate granting original jurisdiction under BCO 33-1, while upholding the portion related to receiving a reference from the Session.

parties: TE Steven Meyerhoff; Chesapeake Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Meyerhoff complained that Chesapeake Presbytery erred in calling a special meeting to receive an initial report from the commission that had been appointed to assume original jurisdiction over Grace Reformed Presbyterian Church. In view of the judgment in Case 2008-11 vacating the commission's original jurisdiction mandate, the SJC found this complaint moot and directed Presbytery to note that in its minutes.

parties: TE Wes White; Presbytery of Siouxlands
observed_synopsis: TE Wes White complained that Siouxlands Presbytery erred when it refused to conduct a BCO 31-2 investigation into whether TE Greg Lawrence was teaching Federal Vision theology contrary to PCA doctrinal standards. The SJC sustained the complaint and remanded the matter to Siouxlands Presbytery for a BCO 31-2 investigation, with a concurring opinion and a single dissenting opinion debating the proper standard of deference owed to the lower court.

Larry Edison et al. v. Southwest Florida Presbytery

parties: Michael McNeil; Chesapeake Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC reported that Michael McNeil’s complaint against Chesapeake Presbytery was found administratively out of order. The published notice does not identify the challenged action or the reason for that ruling, and reports no merits determination, additional relief, or further proceedings for this docket.

parties: Mr. Paul Armes; Southwest Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Southwest Florida Presbytery denied Paul Armes's complaint on the grounds that his excommunication removed his standing; the SJC unanimously remanded the case to the Presbytery after the Presbytery conceded error, holding that even an excommunicated person retains standing to complain against the censure itself.

parties: Mr. Paul Armes; Southwest Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Southwest Florida Presbytery denied Armes's second complaint as a mere restatement of Case 2009-12; the SJC sustained the complaint and remanded, finding the second complaint involved distinct post-censure acts (the trespass notice) that could not be dismissed as identical in substance. A dissenting opinion argued Armes, as an excommunicated person, lacked standing to bring any complaint beyond the limited access afforded under BCO 38-1.

parties: Mr. Michael A. McNeil; Chesapeake Presbytery
observed_synopsis: McNeil complained that Chesapeake Presbytery erred in denying his complaint against the Session's refusal to receive his charges against his wife after the Session had already censured him for abusive behavior; the SJC denied the complaint, applying a standard of great deference to the lower court and finding no clear procedural error.

parties: RE Jerry Koerkenmeier; Illiana Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Illiana Presbytery appointed a Commission with broad powers to 'deal with matters' at Center Grove Presbyterian Church; the SJC found this was constitutional error because the language exceeded proper oversight bounds, but declared the error harmless since the Commission acted only as an investigating committee and the Session itself endorsed the Commission's findings.

parties: RE Roger Phelps; Pacific Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Complainant alleged that Pacific Presbytery erred in not opposing the ordination of Lee Irons as a Ruling Elder at New Life Burbank, given that Pacific Presbytery had previously denied Irons's application as a Teaching Elder candidate; the SJC denied the complaint, holding that each court retains discretion to evaluate candidates for ordination within its jurisdiction and that Presbytery's denial for Teaching Elder did not preclude a Session's ordination of the same man as Ruling Elder.

parties: TE David Brown; Northern California Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Northern California Presbytery adopted an abstract resolution declaring six different views on the diaconate permissible for ministers and Sessions; the SJC sustained the complaints and annulled the resolution, holding that no court may issue binding abstract decrees beyond its proper jurisdictional exercise. A concurring opinion analyzed each of the six diaconal views in detail and set out standards (the GUMP/Kniseley framework) for when diaconal assistant practices are constitutionally permissible.

raw_title: Session of Grace Presbyterian Church v. Northern California Presbytery
parties: Session of Grace Presbyterian Church; Northern California Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Joined with Case 2009-25; the Session of Grace Presbyterian Church complained that views 3, 4, 5, and 6 in Northern California Presbytery's resolution on diaconal practice violated the BCO. The SJC sustained the complaint on the same grounds as 2009-25, annulling the abstract resolution while declining to rule on the constitutional merits of any specific diaconal view.

parties: Mr. Matt Ruff; Nashville Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Matt Ruff complained that Nashville Presbytery failed to conduct an adequate BCO 31-2 investigation and to find a strong presumption of guilt against TE George Grant; the SJC sustained both complaints and remanded, finding the investigation record was incomplete and internally inconsistent, and that conduct described by the Presbytery's own Shepherding Committee as 'sin' required an explanation as to why no strong presumption of guilt existed.

raw_title: Michael A. McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery
parties: Michael A. McNeil; Chesapeake Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC reported McNeil’s complaint against Chesapeake Presbytery as judicially out of order. The published status notice supplies no explanation for that ruling or substantive account of the dispute.

observed_synopsis: The SJC denied a complaint by Kirk Lyons challenging Western Carolina Presbytery's dismissal of charges he filed against TE Craig Bulkeley, finding no clear error in the presbytery's determination that grounds existed under BCO 31-8, 34-2, and 32-20 to decline the charges, though the SJC noted the presbytery erred (non-prejudicially) in denying Lyons standing, since filing BCO 32-2 charges brought him under the court's jurisdiction.

observed_synopsis: Pacific Presbytery was cited and appeared before the SJC regarding exceptions of substance found in its records; the SJC accepted the presbytery's response as acceptable, pending certification that the response was approved by the presbytery.

observed_synopsis: The SJC ruled that McNeil's appeal was judicially out of order because he had not submitted to a regular trial, having refused to enter a plea or appear before Chesapeake Presbytery's Judicial Commission, and that his subsequent censure of suspension from the sacraments eliminated his standing to file further complaints against post-censure actions of the court.

raw_title: Sartorious et al. v. Siouxlands Presbytery
parties: TE Art Sartorious, TE Brian Carpenter, TE Wes White; Siouxlands Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC denied a complaint that Siouxlands Presbytery erred in finding no strong presumption of guilt in TE Joshua Moon after an investigation into allegations that his theological views on Federal Vision topics were heterodox, holding that deference to the presbytery was required absent clear error in the record. The case generated a concurring opinion offering procedural guidance on BCO 31-2 investigations versus BCO 32-2 charges, and a dissenting opinion by RE Haigler arguing the record showed unambiguous heterodoxy warranting a finding of strong presumption of guilt.

observed_synopsis: Mr. McNeil failed to appear at the hearing on Case 2010-01 and had not submitted a written brief. The Panel found the case abandoned and dismissed it.

observed_synopsis: The SJC found Case 2010-24 judicially out of order because Northwest Georgia Presbytery had rescinded the action complained against; a dissenting opinion argued that rescission does not automatically moot a complaint and that Mrs. Wood retained valid grounds related to Presbytery's failure to act.

parties: TE Eliot Lee; Korean Eastern Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Korean Eastern Presbytery erred in dismissing TE Eliot Lee's charges against two Teaching Elders without conducting a trial; the SJC held that once properly drawn charges are filed, a Presbytery must proceed to adjudicate them unless it can demonstrate specific constitutional grounds for dismissal, and remanded the matter to KEP.

parties: Mr. Matt Ruff; Nashville Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found Mr. Ruff's complaint against Nashville Presbytery's failure to investigate a second Teaching Elder to be judicially out of order because the complaint was not filed within 30 days of the August 18, 2010 Presbytery meeting; a concurring objection argued this ruling was inherently unfair as Mr. Ruff was not notified of the meeting or that no action had been taken.

parties: TE Stephen Gonzales; Great Lakes Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Great Lakes Presbytery erred in approving Recommendation 5 of its Judicial Commission's report, which preemptively stated that Presbytery would not recommend or transfer TE Gonzales if he declined to demit or step away from ministry, because such action exceeded Presbytery's authority apart from censure after due judicial process.

parties: Mr. Sang Chul Choi; Korean Central Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Mr. Choi's complaint was found Administratively Out of Order because it was prematurely filed with the General Assembly before Korean Central Presbytery had ruled on his complaint about the Presbytery's refusal to accept his charges.

parties: Mr. Frank Testa; South Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Mr. Testa's complaint against South Florida Presbytery was ruled administratively out of order because South Florida Presbytery had not yet acted on the matter. The SJC adopted the ruling 19 concurring, 1 not qualified, and 4 absent.

raw_title: Spann v. Oak Mountain Presbyterian Church
parties: Susan Elizabeth Spann; Oak Mountain Presbyterian Church
observed_synopsis: Susan Elizabeth Spann filed an appeal alleging Oak Mountain Presbyterian Church committed excommunication without process and spiritual abuse, but the SJC dismissed the appeal as premature because there was no record of a judicial decision by OMPC nor any prior appeal to Evangel Presbytery as required by BCO 42-2. The SJC requested that Evangel Presbytery direct OMPC to provide a written response to Ms. Spann's concerns.

parties: TE Stephen Gonzales; Great Lakes Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found that Great Lakes Presbytery erred in declaring TE Gonzales's second complaint out of order by conflating it with the first complaint (SJC 2010-28), but denied the complaint on the merits because TE Dupee's allegedly offending statement was made in his representative capacity as Committee Chairman, not personally, and therefore could not be the subject of a BCO 31-2 investigation.

raw_title: Sagan et al. v. Covenant Presbytery
parties: TE Paul Sagan et al.; Covenant Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC denied complaints that Covenant Presbytery's MNA Committee exceeded its authority in presenting a report and recommendations concerning the Mississippi Joint Committee on Campus Work, finding that the committee's investigation of the MJCCW structure was a natural extension of its assigned mandate to review campus minister salaries.

raw_title: Gunn et al. v. Covenant Presbytery
parties: TE Grover Gunn et al.; Covenant Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Identical companion case to 2011-03; the SJC denied this complaint by TE Grover Gunn et al. against Covenant Presbytery's handling of its MNA Committee report on the same grounds as 2011-03, with both cases heard together by an expanded panel.

parties: Mr. Young Bae Kim; Korean Capital Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Mr. Kim's complaint was found Administratively Out of Order because it was not filed with the Stated Clerk within 30 days following the last meeting of Korean Capital Presbytery on October 4, 2010.

raw_title: Presbyterian Church in America v. Warrior Presbytery
parties: Presbyterian Church in America; Warrior Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The 39th General Assembly had cited Warrior Presbytery for failure to respond to exceptions of substance in minutes from 2007 and 2009. The SJC reviewed Warrior Presbytery's responses submitted under BCO 10-4 and found them acceptable, resolving the citation.

parties: Mr. Paul Sherfey; James River Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Mr. Sherfey's complaint against James River Presbytery was ruled judicially out of order with defects that cannot be cured, because the bases of his complaint had not been adjudicated by JRP as required by BCO 43-2, and because the complaint to the General Assembly was not timely filed within the 30-day period of BCO 43-3. A concurring opinion by RE Duncan and RE Burnett noted that JRP's commission gave de novo review beyond the Record of the Case and should have narrowly adjudicated whether JRP erred in denying the original complaint.

parties: TE Stephen Jennings; North Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: North Florida Presbytery was found to have erred in restoring deposed minister A. B. Scott to the office of Teaching Elder by a vote of 19-17, which the SJC determined did not satisfy the BCO 34-8 requirement that 'the general sentiment of the Church is strongly in his favor.' The SJC annulled NFP's actions and remanded the case; a lengthy dissent by RE Donahoe argued that BCO 34-8 does not require a super-majority and that the restoration vote is distinct from the evaluation of general sentiment.

parties: TE William Smith; Mississippi Valley Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE William Smith complained against Mississippi Valley Presbytery's excommunication of TE Jeremy Smith who had confessed to adultery and abandoning his family. The SJC sustained one of the five allegations of error, finding that Presbytery incorrectly judged that the minister had 'refused' to appear since he was never formally cited, though the SJC did not annul the censure given other grounds for excommunication.

parties: Mr. Matt Ruff; Nashville Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Mr. Ruff complained that Nashville Presbytery failed to comply with the SJC's prior ruling in Case 2009-28 when it concluded its BCO 31-2 investigation of TE George Grant via a case without process under BCO 38-1. The SJC found Presbytery had authority to use BCO 38-1 but erred in accepting a confession that was almost entirely abstract and did not adequately address particular sins against particular persons, and directed Presbytery to obtain an amended confession and sponsor reconciliation.

raw_title: Sawyers et al. v. Missouri Presbytery
parties: TE Sean Sawyers, et al.; Missouri Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Complainants alleged Missouri Presbytery erred in failing to find a strong presumption of guilt that TE Jeffrey Meyers held views contrary to the Westminster Standards in its BCO 31-2 investigation. The SJC found that MOP erred but declared the case moot because MOP had already conducted a trial of TE Meyers during the pendency of the case before the SJC.

parties: Mr. Paul Sherfey; James River Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC dismissed Case 2012-01 as judicially out of order on the ground that the action complained against was not in the Record of the Case. A dissenting opinion by three members argued the case should have been adjudicated, contending there was a complain able Session action in the record, as the SJC had itself indicated in the earlier related Case 2011-08; a written objection was also filed regarding TE Aquila's participation as panel chairman given his prior advice to the session at issue.

parties: Presbyterian Church in America; Korean Capital Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The 40th General Assembly had cited Korean Capital Presbytery for failure to respond to exceptions of substance in minutes from October 6, 2008. The SJC noted that Korean Capital Presbytery submitted responses approved by the Presbytery under BCO 10-4, and found those responses acceptable.

parties: TE Shawn Keating; Warrior Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Shawn Keating appealed his divestiture without censure by Warrior Presbytery, arguing Presbytery failed to follow BCO 34-10 procedures. The SJC sustained the appeal on procedural grounds, finding that Presbytery erred by proceeding to divestiture without first hearing the minister in his own defense, and voided the divestiture while noting Presbytery remained free to proceed again following proper procedures.

raw_title: Dunn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
parties: TE Dwight Dunn; Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found TE Dwight Dunn's complaint against Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery to be administratively out of order because the complaint was transmitted to a presbytery commission by the Stated Clerk rather than by motion and action of Presbytery, and because the commission's judgment was never brought back to Presbytery for approval as required by BCO 15-3.

parties: RE Gerald Hedman; Pacific Northwest Presbytery
observed_synopsis: RE Gerald Hedman complained that Pacific Northwest Presbytery unconstitutionally adopted five not-guilty verdicts regarding TE Peter Leithart's teachings on baptism, covenants, imputation, justification, and union with Christ. The SJC denied the complaint, finding it was bound by the Record of the Case and that Complainant had not demonstrated clear error on the part of Presbytery, with concurring and dissenting opinions discussing the scope of review, standing, and concerns about Leithart's sacramental theology.

parties: DE Don Bethel; Southeast Alabama Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC ruled Case 2012-06 administratively out of order on two grounds: the complaint was not filed within the required 30-day period under BCO 43-2, and the complainant (a deacon who was not a commissioner to presbytery on the date of the action complained against) lacked standing under BCO 43-1.

parties: TE M. Jay Bennett; Missouri Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC ruled Case 2012-09 administratively out of order because, although the complainant was a PCA member when he filed his original complaint to Presbytery on April 16, 2012, he had transferred to the OPC on April 28, 2012, and therefore lacked standing to bring his complaint to the SJC on August 16, 2012.

raw_title: Steven Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
parties: Steven Hahn; Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Steven Hahn filed multiple complaints against Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery (PMWP) arising from his exclusion from worship at Christ the King Presbyterian Church pending a psychiatric evaluation, his subsequent conviction of three charges by PMWP, and PMWP's refusal to institute process against those he accused. The SJC denied all three complaints (2011-11, 2011-12, 2011-15), finding no clear error in PMWP's exercise of deference to the lower court, guilty verdict, or declination to appoint a prosecutor under BCO 31-8.

Reese and Bech v. Philadelphia Presbytery

observed_synopsis: RE Reese and TE Bech complained that Philadelphia Presbytery erred in declaring their complaint out of order after Presbytery refused to allow any questions of TE Jason Hsu regarding his views on women deacons when approving his transfer to City Line Church. The SJC sustained the complaint, finding that deeming parts of a complaint objectionable is insufficient grounds to rule the whole complaint out of order, though it agreed the proposed amends (removing TE Hsu) were not appropriate.

raw_title: Appeal of TE Charles Tarter v. Evangel Presbytery
parties: TE Charles (Chuck) Tarter; Evangel Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Tarter appealed his deposition by Evangel Presbytery's Judicial Commission for failure to submit to presbytery authority. The SJC sustained multiple specifications of error—including that Presbytery's committee lacked authority to make certain demands, the indictment was inadequate, and hearsay evidence was improperly admitted—vacated the judgment and censure, and remanded the case for constitutionally compliant process or dismissal.

raw_title: RE William G. Mitchell vs. The Presbytery of the Ascension
parties: RE William G. Mitchell; The Presbytery of the Ascension
observed_synopsis: RE Mitchell appealed his indefinite suspension from office as Ruling Elder by the Presbytery of the Ascension, arising from allegations he broke a promise to take a sabbatical from Session and failed in his duties as Clerk of Session. The SJC vacated the judgment on Specification No. 2 (promise-breaking) and remanded for possible new trial, and reversed and dismissed Specification No. 6 (clerk duties) as insufficiently serious to warrant trial.

raw_title: Dunn and Pesnell vs. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
parties: TE Dwight Dunn and TE Darin Pesnell; Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Dunn and TE Pesnell complained that Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery erred in adopting its commission's recommendation to institute process and proceed to trial against TE David Swavely for alleged pastoral and spiritual abuse. The SJC denied the complaint, finding that the Presbytery had sufficient authority to proceed to trial and that the errors alleged did not rise to a reversible level.

raw_title: Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port, Florida v. Presbytery of Southwest Florida
parties: Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port, Florida; The Presbytery of Southwest Florida
observed_synopsis: The SJC sustained the appeal of the Session of FPC North Port from the Presbytery of Southwest Florida's judgment suspending the Session, reversing the judgment in whole and dismissing all charges. The Commission held that Presbytery's citation and trial of the FPC Session for failure to initiate ecclesiastical process against a church member was constitutionally out of order, compounding the same errors identified in Case 2013-07, as Presbytery had failed to follow the required steps of BCO 40-5 before proceeding against the Session.

raw_title: Complaint of the Session of Hope Community Church vs. Central Carolina Presbytery
parties: Session of Hope Community Church; Central Carolina Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The Session of Hope Community Church complained that Central Carolina Presbytery erred in adopting a policy requiring a multi-site session to eventually particularize its second worship site as a distinct new church. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that the BCO expressly vests the Session with authority over the time and place of worship and the Presbytery's mandatory particularization requirement exceeded its constitutional powers and was annulled.

raw_title: Stephen Hahn request concerning Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Stephen Hahn asked the SJC to assume original jurisdiction over Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery. The SJC found Case 2013-05 administratively out of order and did not reach the merits.

raw_title: Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port v. Presbytery of Southwest Florida
parties: Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port; The Presbytery of Southwest Florida
observed_synopsis: The SJC sustained the Session of FPC North Port's complaint that Southwest Florida Presbytery erred when it remanded a previously out-of-order complaint back to the Session and when it directed and instructed the Session to initiate formal ecclesiastical process against a member without following the required steps of BCO 40-5. The Commission held that once the Original CM Complaint was found out of order, there was no matter for Presbytery to carry forward, and any subsequent instructions to the Session to initiate process were null and void.
