parties: Rev. Stuart Latimer; Chicago Metro Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC sustained Rev. Latimer's appeal from his deposition for allegedly pursuing an unbiblical divorce, finding that Presbytery clearly erred because the record contained no conclusive evidence that his divorce filing — made on advice of counsel to protect his children — reflected an intent to divorce rather than a defensive legal measure; two concurring opinions addressed the Presbytery's choice of definite versus indefinite suspension.

parties: G. Rick Marshall; Pacific Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC dismissed the appeal and suspended the lower court's judgment indefinitely because Pacific Presbytery failed to transmit a material part of the Record of the Case — a defect that could not be remedied — and rebuked the Presbytery for failure to preserve and transmit trial testimony.

parties: G. Rick Marshall; Pacific Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found Marshall's complaint judicially out of order on two grounds: that objections raised during a pending judicial case should be reserved for appeal rather than complaint (BCO 32-14; 42-3), and that no complaint is allowable in a judicial case in which an appeal is pending (BCO 43-1). Three commissioners dissented, arguing BCO 32-14 did not apply before trial commenced and that BCO 43-1's exception is limited to pending appeals, not complaints filed before a trial occurs.

parties: TE Stephen Gonzales; Great Lakes Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC sustained TE Gonzales's appeal, reversing and annulling Great Lakes Presbytery's divestiture of him without censure under BCO 34-10, because GLP failed to follow the required procedural steps: it did not record a finding that Gonzales had habitually failed to discharge his official functions, nor determine that his neglect arose only from lack of acceptance to the Church, before proceeding to divestiture. The decision restored Gonzales to good standing in GLP while leaving open GLP's option to pursue proper process under BCO Chapter 31 or 34-10.

parties: RE Warren Jackson; Northwest Georgia Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order because RE Jackson lacked standing as a non-commissioner to the January 2013 Presbytery meeting, but treated his correspondence as a credible BCO 40-5 report of an important delinquency by the Session of Midway Presbyterian Church, remitting the matter to Northwest Georgia Presbytery for constitutional disposition.

raw_title: Aven and Dively v. Ohio Valley Presbytery
parties: TE Don Aven and TE David Dively; Ohio Valley Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Two ministers complained that Ohio Valley Presbytery erred in granting TE Hickey an exception to Larger Catechism 177 regarding admission of covenant children to the Lord's Supper. The SJC neither sustained nor denied the complaint, remanding the case to the Presbytery because the record was insufficient to evaluate the minister's particular expression of his paedocommunion view.

parties: D. G. Sanfacon; Philadelphia Presbytery
observed_synopsis: An inactive ruling elder's complaint to the Session was filed 78 days after the Session action complained against, exceeding the 60-day window of BCO 43-2. The SJC ruled the complaint administratively out of order and voided all subsequent actions.

parties: John Thompson; South Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Thompson's BCO 40-5 application regarding South Florida Presbytery was found administratively out of order and dismissed because it dealt with proceedings in a judicial case in which a complaint had already been filed, precluding review and control under BCO 40-3.

parties: John B. Thompson; South Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC sustained Thompson's complaint, finding that the Granada Session's judicial commission procedurally erred in imposing excommunication for contumacy before trial because Thompson's behavior did not constitute the immediately censurable kind of contumacy under BCO 32-6.b, and that failing to reach a BCO 38-1 agreement should have led to a trial rather than a pre-trial judgment; the SJC annulled the excommunication and restored the matter to its pre-judgment status as of June 26, 2015.

parties: TE Tolivar Wills; Metro Atlanta Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC ruled Wills's complaint against MAP's September 15, 2015 action declaring a prior complaint administratively out of order was itself administratively out of order, because BCO 43-2 requires a complaint to first be made to the court whose act is alleged to be in error, and MAP had not yet had the opportunity to respond; Duncan, Evans, and Donahoe dissented.

parties: TE Chris Gearhart; Chicago Metro Presbytery
observed_synopsis: An unsigned complaint was filed on TE Gearhart's behalf by a third party without standing, and TE Gearhart did not contact the PCA Clerk until 77 days after the Presbytery action (47 days past the BCO 43-3 deadline). The SJC ruled the complaint administratively out of order because it was not timely filed and the complainant did not give unqualified ratification.

raw_title: Flesher and Weekly v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery
parties: RE Steve Flesher and RE Randy Weekly; Metro Atlanta Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found Complaint 2015-03 moot because the issues it raised were adjudicated in the related Appeal 2015-08 (Hardie v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery).

parties: John B. Thompson; South Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: John Thompson filed a BCO 43-1 complaint challenging his indictment while his judicial case was still in process before the Session. The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order because objections to a trial court's actions must be raised by the defendant during the trial or by appeal after final judgment, not by a separate complaint during the pendency of process.

raw_title: BCO 40-5 Application of John B. Thompson re: Granada Presbyterian Church
parties: John B. Thompson; Granada Presbyterian Church / South Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Thompson's BCO 40-5 application alleging grossly unconstitutional proceedings by Granada Presbyterian Church was filed with the SJC before South Florida Presbytery had opportunity to consider it. The SJC dismissed the application as prematurely filed.

raw_title: Presbyterian Church in America vs. South Florida Presbytery (Citation)
parties: Presbyterian Church in America; South Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC reported that South Florida Presbytery responded to the citation issued by the 43rd General Assembly. The SJC found most responses satisfactory, but found one response unsatisfactory (regarding charges against a TE that were not properly processed under BCO 32-2), and noted an additional exception of substance regarding improper divestiture under BCO 46-8.

parties: John B. Thompson; South Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Thompson's complaint to the SJC was prematurely filed before South Florida Presbytery had considered it at its next stated meeting as required by BCO 43-2. The SJC ruled the complaint administratively out of order.

parties: TE John Hardie; Metro Atlanta Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE John Hardie appealed his conviction and indefinite suspension by Metro Atlanta Presbytery's judicial commission, raising seventeen specifications of error under six categories including procedural irregularities, improper evidence, refusal of indulgence, prejudice, and disproportionate censure. The SJC denied the appeal, finding no clear error in MAP's proceedings and upholding the indefinite suspension.

raw_title: Bumgarner v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley
parties: Brad Bumgarner; Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley
observed_synopsis: Bumgarner, a ruling elder who had been deposed in 2012, filed a BCO 40-5 application in 2015 seeking reversal of the censure after having previously withdrawn his complaint and acknowledged it could not be resubmitted. The SJC dismissed the application as administratively out of order because it sought to re-file a withdrawn complaint and because BCO 40-3 prohibits reversal of judicial censures except by appeal or complaint.

parties: TE Andrew Barnes; Heartland Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Heartland Presbytery sustained the transfer of TE Geoff Smith from an OPC presbytery with stated differences on WCF 19 (the law), without adequately considering or disclosing to the full presbytery that the OPC had declared Smith's views outside the system of doctrine and had restricted him from teaching them. The SJC sustained the complaint and remanded to Heartland for further action, with a dissent arguing there was no clear error under BCO 39-3(3).

parties: TE Don Aven; Ohio Valley Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Following the SJC's 2014-01 remand directing Ohio Valley Presbytery to 'hear further' from TE Hickey regarding his stated difference on Larger Catechism 177 (paedocommunion), the SJC denied Aven's complaint that OVP failed adequately to comply, finding that OVP did sufficiently hear further from the minister. A significant dissent argued OVP did not satisfy the specific directives from Case 2014-01.

raw_title: Harwell et al. v. Nashville Presbytery
parties: RE Sam K. Harwell, et al.; Nashville Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC dismissed this complaint as judicially out of order because the Harwell complainants had not first properly filed a complaint with Nashville Presbytery—what they filed with Presbytery was in fact a suggestion of charges or call for investigation under BCO 31-2, not a complaint against a court action—and then filed their SJC complaint directly, bypassing the required step of complaining first to the court whose action is alleged to be in error.

parties: TE Tolivar Wills; Metro Atlanta Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Tolivar Wills complained that Metro Atlanta Presbytery improperly dissolved Grace North Atlanta Church without following formal judicial process under BCO 40-6. The SJC denied the complaint, ruling that BCO 13-9(f) grants presbytery inherent authority to dissolve a church without mandating any specific procedure, and that the record did not demonstrate clear error in MAP's exercise of its discretion and judgment.

parties: TE Arnold Robertstad; North Texas Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order because it was initially filed via e-mail rather than by hard copy, and was filed by hard copy only after the thirty-day deadline had passed, contrary to BCO 43-3 and OMSJC 18.10.b which prohibit e-mail filing. A concurring opinion provided extensive history of the 2012 and 2014 amendments to BCO 43-3.

raw_title: Troxell v. Presbytery of the Southwest
parties: TE Thomas E. Troxell; The Presbytery of the Southwest
observed_synopsis: The SJC partially sustained this complaint, annulling Charge 1 (failure to manage household well relating to a June 2014 divorce) because the 15-month delay before process was instituted in September 2015 violated the BCO 32-20 one-year rule with no evidence the offense had recently become flagrant; other specifications of error were denied, and the improper declaration the TE was 'not in good standing' was sustained but not of a nature to annul other actions.

raw_title: Avery and Lewelling v. Nashville Presbytery
parties: RE John Avery and RE Dale Lewelling; Nashville Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Avery and Lewelling complained against Nashville Presbytery's denial of their complaint about the Shepherding Committee's investigation of TE Jim Bachmann. The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order because the actions complained of were those of a committee rather than a court, and the complaint against November 2015 Presbytery action was untimely under BCO 43-2.

parties: Ms. Laurie Lee Doty; Nashville Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Ms. Doty and 21 others filed charges against a Nashville Presbytery teaching elder first with his congregation's Session (wrong court), then with Nashville Presbytery; Presbytery declined to indict and treated the matter as a report under BCO 31-2 rather than charges. The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order (11-9-2-2) on the ground that Doty lacked standing under BCO 43-1 as a non-member of Nashville Presbytery; a significant dissent argued that her filing of charges gave her standing under prior precedent (Lyons, Ruff, Fordice).

parties: Mr. Mark Fordice; Pacific Northwest Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Fordice complained that Pacific Northwest Presbytery erred by allowing TE Nathan Lewis to confess under BCO 38-1 and closing the matter without adequate process, after its own investigative committee had found a strong presumption of guilt on 18 allegations. The SJC unanimously sustained the complaint and remanded the case to PNW, finding that while use of BCO 38-1 was not itself error, the approved statement of facts was not 'full' as required because it failed to correlate with the underlying allegations.

parties: Korean Northwest Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Korean Northwest Presbytery amended and adopted its responses to SJC exceptions at its April 2017 meeting; the SJC accepted those amended and corrected responses by roll call vote (18 concur, 1 dissent, 1 abstain).

parties: TE Michael Frazier; Nashville Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Frazier complained that Nashville Presbytery erred in finding insufficient evidence to raise a strong presumption of guilt against TE Scott Sauls regarding his teaching on same-sex attraction; the SJC denied the complaint 20-0-1, concluding NP fulfilled its BCO 31-2 investigatory duties, accompanied by several concurring opinions raising procedural and exegetical concerns.

raw_title: Daniels et al. v. Nashville Presbytery
parties: RE Scott Daniels, et al.; Nashville Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC declared the complaint moot by a vote of 13-6; the substantial dissenting opinion by six members argued the Commission provided no rationale for the mootness determination and that no constitutional basis for declaring it moot was established.

parties: TE James Bachmann; Nashville Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Bachmann appealed Nashville Presbytery's decision to amend its judicial commission's recommended censure of admonition to indefinite suspension; the SJC sustained the appeal, finding NP violated BCO 15-3 by dividing the question and amending the JC's judgment, and rendered the decision that should have been rendered by restoring the JC's censure of admonition.

parties: TE Arthur Sartorius; Siouxlands Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Sartorius complained that Siouxlands Presbytery erred in acquitting TE Greg Lawrence on five charges of holding Federal Vision and non-confessional views on baptism, perseverance, and covenant of works at a second trial (2015); the SJC denied the complaint 22-1, holding that the complainant failed to demonstrate clear error in the trial court's factual finding and that BCO 39-3.2 requires great deference to the lower court's verdict. A concurring opinion by RE Donahoe extensively discussed standards of appellate review, defendant testimony supporting the acquittal, and raised concerns about due process rights of acquitted persons.

parties: RE Morris Webster and RE Wayne Fowler; Heritage Presbytery
observed_synopsis: RE Webster and RE Fowler complained that Heritage Presbytery exceeded its authority when it passed a motion advising the Session of New Covenant Presbyterian Church to postpone ordaining a candidate who might be found unqualified due to non-subscription to infant baptism; the SJC denied the complaint 20-0, finding that Presbytery merely offered advice that Session was free to reject and did not impinge on Session's constitutional authority.

parties: RE John Avery; Nashville Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC declared Case 2016-06 to have been abandoned and approved this action without objection.

parties: RE Scott Dailey; Heritage Presbytery
observed_synopsis: RE Dailey complained that Heritage Presbytery erred in upholding its Moderator's ruling that a church member's document was administratively in order as a complaint under BCO 43-3, after the Session had ruled it out of order. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that neither triggering condition of BCO 43-3 was met because the Session's ruling that the document did not qualify as a BCO 43-1 complaint was not equivalent to denying it, and the Session had considered and responded to the matter in a timely manner. A substantial dissent argued for a broader interpretation of 'fails to consider' in BCO 43-3.

parties: Korean Eastern Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC Commission recognized that Korean Eastern Presbytery complied with its citation, provided required materials under BCO 40-1, and referred those materials to the Committee for Review of Presbytery Records.

parties: Korean Southwest Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC Commission unanimously accepted responses from Korean Southwest Presbytery as complying with the SJC citation and forwarded those responses to the Review of Presbytery Records Committee.

parties: Platte Valley Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC Commission unanimously accepted responses from Platte Valley Presbytery as complying with the SJC citation and forwarded those responses and requested minutes to the Review of Presbytery Records Committee.

parties: RE Charles Postles; Heritage Presbytery
observed_synopsis: RE Postles complained that Heritage Presbytery erred in acting on an ad interim committee recommendation to charge a teaching elder with violating ordination vows 6 and 7 and appointing a prosecutor. The SJC denied the complaint, finding that a committee may recommend judicial action without special authorization (distinguishing from a commission under BCO 15-3), that BCO 31-2 procedures were properly followed, and that the language used by Presbytery in its motion was constitutionally sufficient to institute process.

raw_title: Clements v. Blue Ridge Presbytery (Reference and Complaint)
parties: TE Don Clements; Blue Ridge Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Blue Ridge Presbytery requested a reference for the SJC to hear and decide TE Clements' complaint (case 2017-07), but the SJC denied the request for reference, finding the record did not demonstrate sufficient bias, constitutional questions, or unusual difficulty to justify reference under BCO 41-2 or 41-3, directing BRP to hear and decide the complaint itself. Case 2017-07 (the companion complaint) was answered by reference to this decision.

parties: TE Don Clements; Blue Ridge Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Companion complaint to 2017-06; the SJC answered this complaint by reference to its decision denying the request for reference in 2017-06, directing Blue Ridge Presbytery to hear and decide the matter.

raw_title: Appeal of TE James Bachmann v. Nashville Presbytery
Anna Lewis v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley
parties: Anna Lewis; Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley
observed_synopsis: After her session erased her from the roll, Anna Lewis filed a BCO 40-5 report directly with the SJC, alleging the Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley failed to redress the session's alleged failure to give BCO 38-4 notice. The SJC held the filing out of order: under RAO 16-10.c and OMSJC Chapter 15, BCO Chapter 40 matters come to it only by General Assembly referral. It did not decide the merits, but noted that without proper notice Lewis remains a member unless she joined another church. Dissents disputed that limitation and cited past direct reviews.

parties: Geoffrey Durand; Central Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC unanimously ruled that Geoffrey Durand's BCO 31-2 report affecting Christian character was administratively out of order and could not be put in order, as there is no constitutional provision for the SJC to receive a BCO 31-2 report directly.

raw_title: Mapes v. Metropolitan New York Presbytery
parties: RE Glen Mapes, et al.; Metropolitan New York Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found the complaint by RE Glen Mapes et al. not judicially in order because it was rendered moot: the remedy sought (a congregational meeting to vote on leaving the PCA) was accomplished when the presbytery voted to dismiss the congregation and the congregation consented. Three members dissented.

parties: TE David McKay; Central Indiana Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC unanimously ruled the complaint by TE David McKay was administratively out of order because the e-mail transmitted to the clerk of the lower court did not meet BCO 43-3's requirement for proper notice.

parties: Jared Edwards; North Texas Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC ruled the complaint by Jared Edwards was administratively out of order and could not be put in order because the case was never filed with the presbytery or adjudicated below, as required by BCO 42-4 and 43-2.

raw_title: Dodson et al. v. Ohio Presbytery
parties: TE Rhett Dodson, et al.; Ohio Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The Session of Grace PCA in Ohio excommunicated Travis and Sherylyn Dougherty for heresy (Trinitarian partialism) without separately establishing contumacy. Ohio Presbytery reversed the excommunication but failed to impose any new censure or remand the matter to Session; the SJC sustained the complaint in part, finding Presbytery correctly overturned the excommunication for lack of contumacy evidence but erred in leaving the guilty parties with no censure and in mandating the transfer of members to another church.

raw_title: Evans and Pitts et al. v. Arizona Presbytery
parties: TE John F. Evans and RE Alan Pitts, et al.; Arizona Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Arizona Presbytery deposed TE Evans under BCO 38-1 without properly securing his approval of the full statement of facts, as the Investigative Committee's report added additional adverse facts he had not seen or approved. The SJC sustained the complaints of Evans and Pitts et al., annulled the deposition, and remanded the matter to AZP for action consistent with BCO 38-1 requirements; a lengthy concurring opinion by RE Donahoe extensively analyzed BCO 38-1 confession procedures.

parties: Dan and Angelia Crouse; Northwest Georgia Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC denied a complaint by an ordained Deacon whose nomination for re-election was not advanced by the Session, holding that the Session's exercise of discretion in evaluating a candidate's eligibility for office did not constitute clear error requiring reversal. The dissent argued the proper standard of review was BCO 39-3.4 (de novo for constitutional interpretation), not 39-3.3 (great deference), because the Session applied extra-biblical and extra-constitutional attendance standards in blocking re-election.

raw_title: Pitts et al. v. Arizona Presbytery
parties: RE Alan Pitts, et al.; Arizona Presbytery
observed_synopsis: This case was joined with Case 2019-10 (Evans v. Arizona Presbytery) and decided together. RE Pitts and co-complainants challenged the same BCO 38-1 procedural errors in TE Evans's deposition, and the SJC sustained both complaints on the same grounds.

parties: Ms. Colleen Gendy; Central Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC sustained a complaint finding that Central Florida Presbytery erred in ruling that Ms. Gendy lacked standing to complain about her removal from church membership under BCO 38-4, holding that a member facing removal retains standing to challenge that removal. The case was remanded to Presbytery to consider the original complaint regarding whether the Session had properly applied BCO 38-3a and 38-4.

raw_title: Yoo et al. v. Korean Southwest Orange County Presbytery
parties: Mr. Jeawhan Yoo, et al.; Korean Southwest Orange County Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found this complaint administratively out of order and dismissed it because no documentation was received showing the complaint was first made to the presbytery whose act was alleged to be in error, and the proper court for the charges included was the Presbytery.

raw_title: Schrock et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery
parties: TE Daniel Schrock, et al.; Philadelphia Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Daniel Schrock and others complained that Philadelphia Presbytery failed to properly judge and record the nature of TE Larry Smith's views on the continuation of spiritual gifts of prophecy and tongues when it admitted him by transfer, as required by BCO 21-4e,f and RAO 16-3.e.5. The SJC sustained the complaint by a vote of 14-5-2 and remanded the matter to Presbytery to receive a written statement from TE Smith and make a proper determination, with a substantial dissent arguing the Presbytery had in fact complied with the Constitution and that RAO 16-3.e.5 is not part of the BCO.

parties: Dan & Angelia Crouse; Northwest Georgia Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC sustained the complaint, ruling that a Session erred by prescreening and eliminating a deacon's nomination for ruling elder before the mandatory instruction and examination process required by BCO 24-1. The decision held that BCO 24-1's language is mandatory and that sessions cannot add a preliminary vetting step that bypasses the required sequence of instruction and examination.

parties: TE F. Todd Williams; Chesapeake Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Chesapeake Presbytery's PJC attempted to convert a BCO 32 case of process into a BCO 38-1 case without process after TE Williams partially pled guilty, confusing the two distinct procedures. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled the Presbytery's action, finding the conflation of BCO 32 and 38-1 violated the due process rights of the accused.

parties: Mr. James Goggan; Missouri Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Mr. Goggan was excommunicated by a Missouri Presbytery judicial commission after a trial on charges of bearing false witness, perpetuating a faction, and other offenses. The SJC denied his appeal, finding he failed to demonstrate sufficient reason to sustain any of the alleged errors.

raw_title: Presbyterian Church in America v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley
parties: The Presbyterian Church in America (via BCO 40-5 report by unnamed Petitioner); Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley
observed_synopsis: The SJC ruled that the Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley erred in approving a Session's erasure of a member's name from the roll under BCO 38-4 after she pled not guilty to a charge of failing to submit to church government and pursued divorce contrary to the Session's counsel. The SJC found multiple constitutional errors including improper conflation of a not-guilty plea with refusal to submit, failure to consider whether the member would fulfill vows in another branch of the church, failure to notify the member of her erasure, and proceeding to a case without process after dropping formal charges.

parties: Mr. Chandler Fozard; North Texas Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Mr. Chandler Fozard complained that Fort Worth Presbyterian Church's policy restricting the integration of special case felons (including sex offenders) into the congregation violated Scripture. The SJC denied the complaint 20-1, finding the complainant had not demonstrated the Session violated Scripture or the Constitution, while criticizing the Session's arguments from BCO Preliminary Principles 1 and 2 as improper.

parties: TE Neal Ganzel; Central Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Neal Ganzel appealed his conviction and six-month suspension by Central Florida Presbytery for abuse of spiritual authority and related charges. The SJC unanimously sustained both specifications of error, finding that CFP violated BCO 32-20's one-year statute of limitations for most charges and committed numerous procedural missteps that rendered the disciplinary process significantly flawed and prejudicial, reversing the entire censure.

parties: RE William F. Mueller; South Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: RE Mueller complained that the Redlands Community Church Session reaffirmed a practice of fencing the Lord's Table contrary to BCO 58-4, but the SJC found the Session took no action because the relevant motion failed for lack of a second. The complaint was denied, with a concurring opinion emphasizing that BCO 58-4's fencing requirement remains a constitutional obligation.

raw_title: Peter Benyola v. Central Florida Presbytery
parties: Mr. Peter Benyola; Central Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC dismissed this complaint as administratively out of order on two grounds: the complaint was not timely filed within sixty days of the presbytery actions challenged (ordination/installation of teaching elders and approval of labors outside the bounds), and Mr. Benyola lacked standing as he was neither a member of the presbytery nor a commissioner from a member church at the relevant meeting.

parties: TE David McWilliams; Southwest Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The complainant requested to withdraw and abandon his complaint, which the SJC approved unanimously.

parties: Mr. Peter Benyola; Central Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC dismissed this complaint as administratively out of order because Mr. Benyola lacked standing to complain against a presbytery action, as he was neither a teaching elder member of that presbytery nor a ruling elder commissioner representing a member church at the September 18, 2020 meeting where the presbytery considered and denied the complaint.

parties: TE David McWilliams; Southwest Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC dismissed this complaint as administratively out of order because TE McWilliams, who was not the original complainant, attempted to carry to the SJC a complaint that had been filed by TEs Eudaly and Light; BCO 43-3 permits only the original complainant to take a denied complaint to the next higher court.

parties: TE Steven P. Marusich; Central Indiana Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC remanded the case to Central Indiana Presbytery with instructions to appoint a committee to reinvestigate under BCO 31-2, after its non-judicial commission declined to find a strong presumption of guilt against an accused teaching elder. The dissent argued the SJC failed to give proper great deference under BCO 39-3.3 to the presbytery's investigative commission's discretionary judgment declining to indict, and that the BCO does not require the investigative procedures ordered by the Decision.

parties: Mr. Eric Eagle; Savannah River Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC ruled Case 2020-10 administratively out of order as prematurely filed because Presbytery had not yet completed its hearing on the complaint; the complainant's time to elevate was reset.

parties: TE Ryan Speck; Missouri Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Ryan Speck complained that Missouri Presbytery erred in declining to find a strong presumption of guilt against TE Greg Johnson regarding four allegations arising from his involvement in and teaching at the Revoice 2018 conference; the SJC sustained the complaint in part on Issue 1 (particularly regarding Theological Judgments 2, 3, and 5 about terminology, gay identity, and spiritual friendship), denied Issues 2 and 3, and remanded the matter to Missouri Presbytery for a new hearing on specific questions.

parties: TE Aaron Myers; Illiana Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Aaron Myers appealed his conviction on charges of maltreatment of his wife and fits of anger by Illiana Presbytery; the SJC denied the appeal and upheld all four specifications of error arguments raised by the appellant, affirming the indefinite suspension from office and suspension from the sacraments.

raw_title: In the Matter of BCO 34-1 Requests to Assume Original Jurisdiction
parties: Central Georgia Presbytery, Southeast Alabama Presbytery, Savannah River Presbytery (2020 Overtures 2, 4, and 25)
observed_synopsis: The SJC answered BCO 34-1 requests from three presbyteries to assume original jurisdiction by reference to the SJC's prior decisions in Case 2020-12 and Case 2020-05, both involving TE Ryan Speck v. Missouri Presbytery. RE Mel Duncan requested that his negative vote be recorded.

parties: TE Ryan Speck; Missouri Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC sustained in part and denied in part TE Ryan Speck's complaint against Missouri Presbytery's December 2019 adoption of six theological judgments regarding the 2018 Revoice Conference hosted by Memorial Presbyterian Church, ruling that MOP applied an incorrect constitutional standard (BCO 34-5 'vitals of religion') rather than the proper BCO 11-3, 11-4, and 13-9(f) criteria, and failed to take adequate action with respect to erroneous teachings identified by its own committees regarding terminology (TJ 2), the 'gay beneath the gay' (TJ 3), and spiritual friendships (TJ 5); the matter was remanded to MOP with instructions for a new hearing. Dissenting opinions were filed by RE John D. Pickering and TE David F. Coffin, Jr., who argued that the SJC improperly raised an issue not presented by either party in violation of BCO 39-3.1.

raw_title: Gordon v. Southern New England Presbytery
parties: Brian Paul Gordon; Southern New England Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Mr. Gordon was excommunicated by a PCA Session after his former OPC congregation joined the PCA against his expressed wishes; he contended the PCA Session lacked jurisdiction over him. The SJC majority denied his appeal affirming the excommunication, while a four-member dissent argued the SJC should have ruled the case out of order for lack of jurisdiction and standing, as Gordon never voluntarily became a PCA member.

parties: TE Rankin Wilbourne; Pacific Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Pacific Presbytery's judicial commission read a prejudicial six-page report prior to TE Wilbourne's BCO 38-1 confession of guilt, then deposed him; the SJC sustained the complaint, annulled the deposition, and recommended treating his 17-month effective suspension as definite suspension from office. Complaints 2020-08 and 2020-09 by fellow TEs and the Session of Pacific Crossroads Church were sustained by reference to this decision.

raw_title: Gendall, Hightower, and Lien v. Pacific Presbytery
parties: TE Shawn Gendall, TE Russell Hightower, and TE Timothy Lien; Pacific Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Three Teaching Elders complained against Pacific Presbytery's handling of TE Wilbourne's BCO 38-1 confession and subsequent deposition. The SJC sustained the complaints by reference to its decision in Case 2020-07.

raw_title: Sean Ozbalt and Erin Barr v. Pacific Presbytery
parties: RE Sean Ozbalt and RE Erin Barr; Pacific Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Session members of Pacific Crossroads Church filed a complaint against Pacific Presbytery's handling of TE Wilbourne's deposition. The SJC sustained the complaint by reference to its decision in Case 2020-07.

parties: Mr. Stuart Michelson; Northwest Georgia Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC ruled Case 2021-01 administratively out of order as prematurely filed because Presbytery had not yet completed its hearing on the complaint; the complainant's time to elevate was reset.

parties: F. Todd Williams; Chesapeake Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Williams appealed Chesapeake Presbytery's approval of his deposition from office and suspension from the Sacraments after trial on three charges (failure to manage household, slander, inappropriate behavior). The SJC denied all five specifications of error and upheld the Presbytery's decision in whole.

parties: Christian Michelson and Stuart Michelson; Northwest Georgia Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order because it targeted actions of a congregational meeting rather than any act or decision of a court of the Church, as required by BCO 43-1. A dissenting opinion by RE Jack Wilson and seven others argued that the Complainants had sufficiently identified an act of the Session (calling the congregational meeting with the stated purposes) to present a justiciable issue.

parties: Phil Dudt; Northwest Georgia Presbytery
observed_synopsis: RE Dudt was convicted and suspended from office by the Midway Presbyterian Church Session for emailing the congregation an SJC decision and expressing disagreement with a Session action, which the Session characterized as violating his ordination vows. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversing in whole and rendering a verdict of not guilty, finding that the Session had no constitutional authority to forbid Dudt from distributing the SJC decision and that the charges of false statements were not proven. A concurring opinion by several judges cautioned against elders emailing congregations in disagreement with Session decisions.

parties: RE Lindsey Tippins; Northwest Georgia Presbytery
observed_synopsis: On a BCO 40-5 request, the SJC advised that the matter should be referred to the General Assembly's Review of Presbytery Records Committee, with three members dissenting.

raw_title: DeJong v. Session of Village Seven Presbyterian Church
parties: RE Donavon J. DeJong; Session of Village Seven Presbyterian Church
observed_synopsis: The SJC sustained in part and denied in part RE DeJong's complaint against Session of Village Seven Presbyterian Church (Rocky Mountain Presbytery), upholding Session's creation of a Judicial Commission and its recommendation to remove term limit restrictions for ruling elders, but annulling Session's creation of a Governance Commission because two provisions of the governing document unconstitutionally allowed the commission to function like the Session itself, exceeding the limits placed on commissions by BCO 15-1.

raw_title: Eudaly and Light v. Southwest Florida Presbytery
parties: TE Dustyn Eudaly and TE Steven Light; Southwest Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC ruled Case 2021-05 administratively out of order because the complainants had affiliated with another branch of the visible church on February 9, 2020, losing PCA jurisdiction and therefore lacking standing to file the complaint.

raw_title: RE J. Lance Acree v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
parties: RE J. Lance Acree; Tennessee Valley Presbytery
observed_synopsis: RE Acree attempted to complain directly to Tennessee Valley Presbytery about action taken at a meeting where he was not a commissioner. The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order because BCO 43-1 gave him no standing to complain against that action. It added that Presbytery should itself have declined to adjudicate the complaint.

raw_title: In the Matter of Korean Southwest Orange County Presbytery
parties: Korean Southwest Orange County Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC cited Korean Southwest Orange County Presbytery regarding unanswered RPR exception-of-substance citations from 2015-2018. The SJC extended a deadline for Presbytery to file adopted responses by April 1, 2022, threatening a called hearing if not met.

parties: Gary Lee Miller; Ohio Valley Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Mr. Miller complained that the Session of Grace and Peace PCA erred in refusing to remove 14 items (stained glass windows, etchings, banners) he alleged violated the Second Commandment. The SJC denied the complaint, finding no clear error in the Session's judgment that the items were not images of the Triune God and were not used as aids in worship.

parties: Eric Eagle, et al.; Savannah River Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Complaint by Eric Eagle and others against Savannah River Presbytery, found administratively out of order by the SJC Officers because the complaint was not timely filed within thirty days of the later of the SJC's notification (October 21, 2021) or Presbytery's ruling (October 20, 2020), as required by BCO 43-3. The case was dismissed on a unanimous 19-0-0 vote.

raw_title: Park et al. v. Korean Central Presbytery
parties: TE Brian Park et al.; Korean Central Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC sustained a complaint against Korean Central Presbytery for administering a censure to a teaching elder before an indictment was drawn, in violation of BCO 32-3, and declared the underlying matter moot given that events occurred 21 years prior and the victim declined to participate. A concurring opinion argued the case should have been remanded to Presbytery for further action, and a dissenting opinion objected to declaring the case moot.

raw_title: Herron et al. v. Central Indiana Presbytery
parties: TE Herron et al.; Central Indiana Presbytery
observed_synopsis: This complaint was postponed pending resolution of Case 2022-10 (PCA v. Herron trial) per the SJC's June 2022 instruction in Case 2021-06, and the SJC ruled it be decided by reference to the April 5, 2023 Final Decision in Case 2022-10.

raw_title: Barber et al. v. Central Indiana Presbytery
parties: RE Dan Barber et al.; Central Indiana Presbytery
observed_synopsis: This complaint was postponed pending resolution of Case 2022-10 (PCA v. Herron trial) per the SJC's June 2022 instruction in Case 2021-06, and the SJC ruled it be decided by reference to the April 5, 2023 Final Decision in Case 2022-10.

raw_title: Herron et al. v. Central Indiana Presbytery
parties: TE Daniel Herron et al.; Central Indiana Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC denied most specifications of a complaint filed by TE Herron and others against Central Indiana Presbytery's investigative and suspension procedures, but sustained the complaint on the point that Presbytery improperly denied Herron access to Presbytery minutes while under process. The decision includes extensive discussion of pre-trial BCO 43-1 complaints ('interlocutory appeals') and the proper scope of BCO 31-10 administrative suspensions.

raw_title: Presbyterian Church in America v. TE Daniel Herron
parties: Presbyterian Church in America; TE Daniel Herron
observed_synopsis: The SJC conducted a full 42-hour trial of TE Daniel Herron of Central Indiana Presbytery on charges arising from allegations of sexual harassment and bullying, referred to the SJC by CIP under BCO 41. The SJC acquitted TE Herron on all charges, removed all censures and administrative suspensions imposed by CIP, and restored him to good standing as a PCA minister.

raw_title: BCO 34-1 Petitions re: Central Indiana Presbytery
parties: Petitioners (re: Central Indiana Presbytery); Central Indiana Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC decided the BCO 34-1 petitions regarding Central Indiana Presbytery by reference to the April 5, 2023 final decision in Case 2022-10 (PCA v. Herron), having previously postponed consideration of these petitions until after the Herron trial concluded.

parties: Petitioners (Southeast Alabama Presbytery, Grace Presbytery via Overtures 36 and 37); Missouri Presbytery / TE Greg Johnson
observed_synopsis: Two overtures from Southeast Alabama and Grace Presbyteries sought GA assumption of original jurisdiction over TE Greg Johnson of Missouri Presbytery for alleged doctrinal errors; the SJC dismissed the petitions (22-1) because TE Johnson and Memorial Presbyterian Church withdrew from the PCA in December 2022, depriving the PCA of jurisdiction.

parties: Mr. Wade Miller; Hills & Plains Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found Mr. Miller's complaint administratively out of order (22-0) because he filed it with the Session six months after the Session's action (May 19, 2021), well beyond the 60-day deadline required by BCO 43-1.

parties: TE Sung Bok Oh; Korean Southeast Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Sung Bok Oh withdrew his complaint against Korean Southeast Presbytery on August 29, 2022.

parties: RE Terry Murdock; South Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order (23-0) because complainant RE Terry Murdock died on November 15, 2022, and no other party had joined the original complaint.

raw_title: Michelson et al. v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
parties: Mr. Stuart Michelson et al.; Northwest Georgia Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found the complaint out of order and moot (23-0) because the Session had dismissed all charges against the three Ruling Elders involved and those REs voluntarily resigned and had their calls dissolved on July 23, 2022, settling the underlying dispute.

raw_title: Peter Benyola v. Central Florida Presbytery (three complaints)
observed_synopsis: Peter Benyola's three complaints against Central Florida Presbytery were found administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order because he was no longer a member of a PCA congregation and therefore lacked standing. The SJC did not reach the merits.

raw_title: Herron & Baysinger v. Central Indiana Presbytery
parties: TE Herron & RE Baysinger; Central Indiana Presbytery
observed_synopsis: This complaint was postponed pending resolution of Case 2022-10 (PCA v. Herron trial) per the SJC's June 2022 instruction in Case 2021-06, and the SJC ruled it be decided by reference to the April 5, 2023 Final Decision in Case 2022-10.

raw_title: Wilson et al. v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
parties: Mr. Derek Wilson et al. (Concerned Members of Covenant Presbyterian Church, Issaquah, WA); Pacific Northwest Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found the complaint judicially out of order (20-2) because BCO 43-1 permits complaints only against acts of a court of the church, not against actions taken in a congregational meeting; the case involved complainants who alleged minor communicant members were wrongly prevented from voting on accepting their associate pastor's resignation, with concurring and dissenting opinions extensively addressing the question of minor communicant suffrage rights and the scope of BCO 43 jurisdiction.

raw_title: Klett et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery
parties: TE Fred Klett et al.; Philadelphia Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC sustained a complaint against Philadelphia Presbytery for failing to find that TE Larry Smith's views affirming continuing gifts of prophecy and tongues (as a 'third category of revelation' beyond special and general revelation) were out of accord with the fundamentals of the system of doctrine because hostile to it, as required by BCO 21-4.f. The case continues past this window's end page.

parties: TE Craig Sheppard; Highlands Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Craig Sheppard complained that Highlands Presbytery erred by conflating judicial and pastoral procedures after finding a strong presumption of guilt, and by failing to institute process within one year as required by BCO 32-20. The SJC sustained both issues, holding that BCO 31-2 mandates process upon finding a strong presumption of guilt, and that Presbytery was debarred from prosecution because the alleged offense occurred in 2017 and timely process was never instituted; three members dissented on the BCO 32-20 issue, arguing it was not a true statute of limitations and that the matter was never a 'case of scandal.'

raw_title: Crouse et al. v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
parties: Crouse et al.; Northwest Georgia Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found this complaint against Northwest Georgia Presbytery out of order and moot because the Session had dismissed all charges and the ruling elders who were subjects of process had voluntarily resigned and had their calls dissolved before the SJC acted. The complaint was accordingly dismissed unanimously.

raw_title: Biese et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
parties: TE Ryan Biese et al.; Tennessee Valley Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The Complainants withdrew this Complaint on July 18, 2022, and the SJC noted such on October 20, 2022. No substantive decision was issued.

raw_title: Harrell et al. v. Covenant Presbytery
parties: Mr. Paul Harrell et al. (seven members of Christ Redeemer PCA); Covenant Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Seven members of a PCA mission church were tried and censured by a provisional Session for opposing the organizing minister's continuation as permanent pastor. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed the convictions, holding that the indictments lacked required specificity under BCO 32-5, that the accused had no sinned against the fifth or ninth commandment by expressing opinions about ministerial suitability, and that the right to choose a pastor belongs to the congregation—not the provisional Session. A concurring opinion addressed indictment requirements, standard of review in appeals, and congregational rights in mission church minister selection.

raw_title: RE David Snoke v. Pittsburgh Presbytery
parties: RE David Snoke; Pittsburgh Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order and unable to be put in order because RE Snoke lacked standing to file a complaint against presbytery action, as he was not a commissioner from his church to the presbytery meeting where the challenged action occurred. The SJC voted 20-1 to dismiss (Sartorius dissenting).

parties: Peter Benyola; Central Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order because Mr. Benyola was no longer a member of any PCA congregation and thus lacked standing. The SJC approved the dismissal unanimously 23-0.

raw_title: Benyola v. Central Florida Presbytery (three complaints)
parties: Mr. Peter Benyola; Central Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC found all three complaints by Mr. Peter Benyola against Central Florida Presbytery administratively out of order (23-0) because Benyola was no longer a member of any PCA congregation and thus lacked standing.

parties: TE David Senters; Savannah River Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE David Senters complained that Savannah River Presbytery erred by judging TE Stamberg's stated difference with WCF 21.3 regarding the gift of tongues as 'not a difference' during a transfer examination. The SJC denied the procedural part of the complaint but sustained the confessional part, finding it was error to conclude Stamberg's view on continuing tongues was not a difference with WCF 1.1 and 1.6, and remanded to Presbytery for further action.

parties: RE Tom Turner; South Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: RE Tom Turner complained against South Florida Presbytery's action finding the Session of Cross Community Church guilty of important delinquencies related to alleged sexual abuse incidents involving the pastor's sons, without formal judicial process. The SJC denied the complaint as to Presbytery's right to investigate under BCO 40-4, but sustained it as to the finding of guilt and imposed censures, holding that formal judicial process (indictment, plea, and trial) under BCO 40-6 was required before findings of guilt could be entered, and remanded to Presbytery.

parties: TE Michael Woodham; South Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Michael Woodham complained that South Florida Presbytery erred by excommunicating a Teaching Elder it had previously deposed without first assigning him to membership in a particular church as required by BCO 46-8. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that Presbytery retained jurisdiction over a deposed minister until transfer to a local church was completed, and that Presbytery's efforts to implement BCO 46-8 showed no clear error; two concurring opinions (RE Donahoe and RE Eggert) offered alternative reasoning regarding the scope of Presbytery's residual jurisdiction.

parties: Mrs. Kristin Hann; Pee Dee Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC dismissed Mrs. Hann's complaint against Pee Dee Presbytery because she lacked standing, not being subject to the jurisdiction of the Presbytery. The ruling noted that Presbytery's ongoing investigation was not stayed by this ruling.

parties: RE John Martinez and RE Jesse Cook; Pacific Presbytery
observed_synopsis: REs Martinez and Cook complained that Pacific Presbytery erred by tasking its Shepherding Committee to follow up with Valley Presbyterian Church's Session after a dispute about doxologies in worship, alleging this exceeded Presbytery's jurisdictional authority. The SJC denied the complaint on Issue 1 (finding no BCO violation in the visitation itself) but sustained it on Issue 2, concluding Presbytery made clear errors of judgment by sending the Shepherding Committee without sufficiently clear instructions or adequate notice.

parties: Mr. Timothy Psiaki; Pacific Northwest Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Mr. Psiaki complained that Covenant Presbyterian Church's Session erred in installing officers elected at a congregational meeting that excluded communicant members under age 18 from voting, in violation of the BCO. The SJC sustained the complaint (15-5), holding that all communicant members have a constitutional right to vote in officer elections regardless of age, and that church bylaws may not override BCO provisions; multiple dissenting opinions argued that BCO 20-3 and 24-3's phrase 'good and regular standing' permits local sessions to establish reasonable minimum voting ages.

raw_title: BCO 40-5 Matter re Metropolitan New York Presbytery
parties: General Assembly (via Committee on Review of Presbytery Records); Metropolitan New York Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC, acting on a BCO 40-5 reference from the 50th General Assembly, remitted this matter to Metropolitan New York Presbytery with an injunction to complete its work dealing with TE Higgins and the Session of Trinity Presbyterian Church (Rye, NY) regarding the unconstitutional practice of allowing a woman to expound Scripture in place of a sermon in public worship. The SJC's ruling included a 'Further Note on Procedure' questioning the constitutionality of the Assembly's direct referral to the SJC without first following the multi-step process prescribed by RAO 16-10.c, prompting multiple concurring and dissenting opinions.

raw_title: BCO 40-5 Matter re Northwest Georgia Presbytery
parties: General Assembly (RPR); Northwest Georgia Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC, pursuant to citation by the 50th General Assembly under BCO 40-5, found that Northwest Georgia Presbytery erred egregiously in approving calls and installing three candidates as associate pastors through a constitutionally deficient election process (slate voting, standing vote, failure to record number of voters present). The SJC stayed all further proceedings and declined to annul the installations, finding no PCA precedent for such relief.

raw_title: Tom Turner v. South Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: RE Tom Turner challenged South Florida Presbytery's handling of matters involving Cross Community Church and the discipline of its pastor after the church voted to disaffiliate from the PCA. The SJC ruled the complaints administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order for lack of standing; two commissioners dissented.

raw_title: Tom Turner v. South Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Case 2023-17 was adjudicated with Case 2023-15. The SJC ruled Tom Turner's complaints administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order for lack of standing after Cross Community Church disaffiliated from the PCA; two commissioners dissented.

parties: TE Jared Huffman; Tennessee Valley Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Huffman filed an appeal after the 50th GA amended BCO 38-1 to change the remedy from complaint to appeal, but his case originated and was nearly complete under the prior rule allowing complaint. The SJC found the case judicially out of order and remanded to Tennessee Valley Presbytery to adjudicate as a complaint under the then-existing rule, resetting the clock for presbytery action.

parties: Mrs. Kappie Reynolds; Pee Dee Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC dismissed Mrs. Reynolds's complaint against Pee Dee Presbytery as untimely, finding it was filed more than sixty days after the Session action in question. The ruling expressly reserved questions about whether she might bring charges as an injured party under BCO 31-5.

raw_title: Biese et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
parties: TE Ryan Biese, RE Nathan Bowers, RE Wil Davis (et al.); Tennessee Valley Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Tennessee Valley Presbytery approved without exception Session minutes planning a youth group Super Bowl Party on Sunday; the SJC denied the complaint because the record was insufficient to find Presbytery erred in its constitutional interpretation. A dissent by RE Eggert argued the complaint was judicially out of order because the SJC lacks constitutional authority to review a presbytery's session-records review decisions under BCO 40-2 and 40-3.

raw_title: Knox Baird et al. v. Grace Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Knox Baird and other elders challenged Grace Presbytery's handling of complaints, BCO 40-5 review requests, document demands, and a stay of pending trials arising from conflict at First Presbyterian Church of Hattiesburg. The SJC sustained the complaints in the main, rejected one specification, and did not reach another; concurring opinions were recorded.

parties: TE John Evans; Arizona Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE John Evans appealed Arizona Presbytery's vote to divest him of his office without censure under BCO 34-10, after he had already affiliated with the Evangelical Presbyterian Church in England and Wales and notified the Presbytery of his withdrawal. The SJC unanimously sustained the appeal and reversed the Presbytery's action, holding that Evans had withdrawn from Presbytery's jurisdiction under BCO 38-3a before the divestiture proceedings began, and instructed the Presbytery to record the irregularity, acknowledge his new membership, and remove his name from the roll.

raw_title: Knox Baird et al. v. Grace Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Case 2023-08 was adjudicated with Case 2023-06 in the Baird complaints against Grace Presbytery. The SJC sustained the complaints in the main, rejected one specification, and did not reach another; concurring opinions were recorded.

parties: TE Aaron Myers; Illiana Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Aaron Myers appealed Illiana Presbytery's decision to elevate his censures from indefinite suspension from office and from the Sacraments to excommunication and deposition, without any additional judicial process. The SJC sustained the appeal 21-1, holding that due process principles require some form of process before censure may be elevated, though the majority held that full de novo judicial process was not required; the sole dissent (RE Eggert) argued that Traditional Process under the BCO Rules of Discipline was required, and a concurring opinion (Sartorius) also argued for full BCO process.

raw_title: Baird et al. v. Grace Presbytery
parties: TE Knox Baird et al. (Session members of First Presbyterian Church, Hattiesburg, MS); Grace Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC sustained multiple complaints brought by elders of First Presbyterian Church Hattiesburg against Grace Presbytery's Commission and Committee, finding: the Blue Hen complaint was moot and never properly filed; the Commission improperly directed the Clerk to produce personal communications beyond official records; Presbytery improperly directed the Session to inform the congregation; and the Commission's stay of pending trials was unconstitutional because BCO 40-5 requires citation of the lower court before any stay can be imposed. Issue 5 (appointment of Committee for BCO 40-5 Reports) was denied.

parties: Mr. Tom Turner; South Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC ruled RE Tom Turner's complaints administratively out of order for lack of standing, because Cross Community Church had voted to disaffiliate from the PCA on February 12, 2023, rendering Turner no longer a PCA member. Two members dissented, arguing CCC should have been afforded hearing and formal process before being denied access to PCA courts.

parties: TE Andrew Flatgard; Metro Atlanta Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Flatgard was deposed by Metro Atlanta Presbytery on three charges related to conduct during his marital separation and divorce; the SJC sustained his appeal 14-3, finding the Record insufficient to support a guilty verdict and censure on the charges of failing to maintain elder qualifications, failing to love his wife, and failing to uphold ordination vows. The case generated extensive concurring and dissenting opinions debating appellate deference standards under BCO 39-3.2, 39-3.3, and 39-3.4.

parties: TE Craig Bulkeley and TE Skip Gillikin; Highlands Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TEs Bulkeley and Gillikin complained that Highlands Presbytery refused to record their dissent against Presbytery's act of recording a letter from the Arden Presbyterian Session affirming the Martins' Christian character. The SJC denied the complaint but went further, annulling Presbytery's recording of the Session letter as contrary to BCO 14-7 and the finality of the prior Sheppard decision (Case 2022-04), generating multiple concurring and dissenting opinions about the SJC's authority to reach issues not raised by the parties.

parties: TE Ian Sears; Nashville Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Ian Sears appealed his deposition by Nashville Presbytery, which handled the case as a BCO 38-1 case without process after he signed a written confession of guilt for two incidents of sexual misconduct in 2010 and 2011. The SJC unanimously denied the appeal on all five specifications of error, affirming the Presbytery's judgment and the validity of the BCO 38-1 process, including its procedures for drafting the confession and refusing to allow Sears to withdraw it after censure was imposed.

parties: RE John Martinez; Pacific Presbytery
observed_synopsis: RE Martinez complained that Pacific Presbytery erred by sustaining a complaint against the Valley Presbyterian Church Session's decision to close worship with benedictions rather than doxologies. The SJC sustained the complaint 19-1, holding that the Session had constitutional authority under BCO 12-5.e to make this liturgical decision and that it was not a clear error of judgment or discretion.

raw_title: Kang et al. v. Korean Central Presbytery
parties: TE Samuel Kang, et al.; Korean Central Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Three Teaching Elders complained that Korean Central Presbytery clearly erred in declining to indict a Teaching Elder after a BCO 31-2 investigation into allegations of financial impropriety, spiritual abuse, and physical abuse. The SJC held that KCP did not clearly err, given the age of the allegations and the deference owed to lower courts on factual and discretionary matters; the dissent argued that KCP's investigation was constitutionally deficient for failing to exercise due diligence.

parties: TE Sam Jung Suh; Korean Southeastern Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Sam Jung Suh appealed his indefinite suspension by Korean Southeastern Presbytery following a trial on charges of financial misconduct. The SJC reversed the conviction in whole, finding that the pre-investigative and BCO 31-2 investigation phases were marred by grave constitutional errors including failure to comply with BCO 27-5, failure to demand satisfactory explanations from TE Suh, improper expansion of the investigation, and absence of a valid antecedent condition necessary to institute process; multiple dissents argued the SJC should have deferred to the lower court's factual findings and trial verdict.

raw_title: William Mueller v. South Florida Presbytery
parties: Mueller; South Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The complaint was withdrawn by agreement of the complainant, the Presbytery Clerk, and the Chairman of Presbytery's Judicial Commission on December 21, 2023. The SJC approved the request and remanded the matter to Presbytery without instructions and without prejudice.

parties: Ms. Emily Hyland; Chicago Metro Presbytery
observed_synopsis: A terminated church employee filed a complaint against Chicago Metro Presbytery after Presbytery declined to indict the pastors she accused, but Presbytery ruled her complaint out of order for lack of standing under BCO 43-1. The SJC, voting 12-12, left the Presbytery's decision standing, finding the complaint judicially out of order because the complainant lacked standing to file a BCO 43-1 complaint against Presbytery.

parties: TE Andy Moehn; Westminster Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Andy Moehn complained that Westminster Presbytery erred in its BCO 31-2 investigation of his wife Kacey Moehn regarding alleged desertion and in declaring the question of biblical divorce grounds moot. The SJC sustained the complaint 21-1-0, finding that Presbytery used an extra-confessional interpretation of WCF 24.6 requiring excommunication before desertion grounds could apply, dismissed relevant evidence, and improperly adjudicated TE Moehn's role in the marriage breakdown without due process; the SJC annulled Presbytery's Recommendations 1 and 3 and found a new investigation was not in order since Mrs. Moehn had left PCA jurisdiction.

raw_title: Gozé v. Hills and Plains Presbytery
parties: Mr. Paul Gozé; Hills and Plains Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC dismissed the appeal as judicially out of order because it was not timely filed within 30 days of notification of the Session's decision per BCO 42-4. RE Jim Eggert filed a dissent arguing that the 30-day period never began because the Session never reduced its decision to writing and delivered it in a prescribed manner, so the appeal should have been deemed timely.

parties: TE Richard Colquitt; Houston Metro Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Colquitt complained that Houston Metro Presbytery's Judicial Commission erred in ruling the Gleason Complaint out of order. The SJC answered Colquitt's Complaint by reference to its ruling in Case 2024-02 (Gleason v. Houston Metro Presbytery), finding that the BCO 43 complaint process is not a proper avenue for accusations, and denied the complaint 21-0-0.

parties: RE William Mueller; South Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: RE Mueller complained that the Redlands Community Church Session erred in allowing Alcoholics Anonymous to use church facilities for weekly meetings, ultimately reaching the SJC after the Session's 14-month failure to consider the complaint and South Florida Presbytery's denial. The SJC denied the complaint, finding AA's use of church property was a matter of Session discretion under BCO 12-5 that did not rise to clear constitutional error, while expressing concern about the Session's lengthy failure to act on the original complaint.

parties: RE John Harris; Wisconsin Presbytery
observed_synopsis: RE Harris, as a Presbytery prosecutor, complained that Wisconsin Presbytery's Judicial Commission erred in dismissing both indictments against a pastor for alleged pastoral care failures. The SJC denied the complaint 18-4-0, finding the JC's dismissal of Indictment 1 under BCO 32-20 (passage of time) was within its discretion despite noting some troubling reasoning by JC members, and that the dismissal of Indictment 2 was authorized because the charge arose from a private offense never brought through proper process; four members dissented as to Indictment 1, arguing the JC clearly erred by conducting a de facto trial with only the accused's unsworn testimony.

parties: Mr. Greg Gleason; Houston Metro Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Mr. Gleason filed a BCO 43 complaint alleging the Session sinned by approving a Personnel Committee Statement read to the congregation regarding an associate pastor's call dissolution. The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order and unable to be put in order because BCO 43 complaints are not a constitutionally permissible avenue for processing accusations of individual sin or requiring repentance from a church court, as complaints address errors of courts rather than sins of individuals.

parties: TE Charles DeWitt; Nashville Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE DeWitt requested withdrawal of his appeal against Nashville Presbytery on November 21, 2024. The SJC dismissed the case per the Appellant's request.

parties: Mr. Peter Benyola; Central Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: Mr. Benyola filed a complaint against Central Florida Presbytery but lacked standing as a non-member of any PCA congregation (BCO 43-1). The SJC dismissed the complaint as administratively out of order, controlled by its prior decisions in Cases 2022-17, 18, and 19 involving the same complainant, voted 21-0-0 with 2 absent and 1 disqualified.

raw_title: Gozé v. Hills and Plains Presbytery
parties: Paul Gozé; Hills and Plains Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC reviewed the complaint and found it administratively out of order and unable to be put in order because it was not a complaint against an act of a court (the Session).

parties: TE Kevin Bigelow; North Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: TE Kevin Bigelow complained against multiple actions of North Florida Presbytery related to the dissolution of his call as Assistant Pastor of Christ Church East (where he was also serving as planting pastor at Christ Church Beaches). The SJC sustained the complaint in part (22-0-0), finding that Presbytery erred in ruling four of Bigelow's five complaints out of order; however, after reviewing the substance of all five complaints, the SJC denied each on the merits, concluding Presbytery committed no clear error in dissolving the call, that no congregational vote of CCB was constitutionally required, and that no formal discipline without process had occurred.

raw_title: Presbyterian Church in America v. South Coast Presbytery
parties: Presbyterian Church in America; South Coast Presbytery
observed_synopsis: This case arose from direction of the 51st General Assembly based on CRPR recommendations, citing South Coast Presbytery for a pattern of noncompliance with minute exceptions. The SJC unanimously concluded SCP had fully complied with the August 12, 2024 Citation, while noting it took no position on the contents of the responses.

parties: Ms. Jennifer Bigelow; North Florida Presbytery
observed_synopsis: The SJC ruled the complaint out of order because the complainant, Ms. Jennifer Bigelow, was not a member of the Presbytery against whose action she complained, and therefore lacked standing to file a BCO 43-1 complaint. The decision was unanimous at 23-0-0 with 1 absent.

raw_title: Mark Hertenstein v. James River Presbytery
TE H.L. Webb and TE T. Miller vs. Pacific Presbytery [ M3GA (1975): 48-50]. Dismissed
observed_synopsis: Judicial complaint by Rev. Harold L. Webb and Rev. Thomas Miller against Pacific Presbytery regarding its August 4, 1975 meeting conducted without the constitutionally required quorum of three teaching and three ruling elders. The Committee on Judicial Business determined the actions were irregular but recommended dismissal after Pacific Presbytery met in duly constituted session on September 10, 1975, with proper quorum and ratified all actions from the August 4 meeting.

The Standing Judicial Commission affirmed that Presbytery of Western Carolina did not err in conducting its BCO 31-2 investigation of accusations against TE Craig Bulkeley or in finding no strong presumption of guilt. The SJC found no constitutional error in Presbytery's procedures and gave great deference to the lower court's discretionary judgment, noting that BCO 31-2 does not mandate specific procedures for investigations. The SJC also held that complainants Kirk Lyons and Robert Woodward lacked standing to bring complaints under BCO 43-1 and 11-4.

Kirk Lyons and others complained that Western Carolina Presbytery erred when it did not find a strong presumption of guilt against TE Craig Bulkeley in a 31-2 investigation, and violated due process by failing to interview the accusing parties. The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaint in part, finding that the Presbytery had denied the complainants due process by not allowing them to present evidence before finding no strong presumption of guilt.

The cases were combined with Case 2009-5 (TE Martin Payne complaint) due to similar circumstances.

observed_synopsis: The SJC, pursuant to citation by the 50th General Assembly under BCO 40-5, found that Northwest Georgia Presbytery erred egregiously in approving calls and installing three candidates as associate pastors through a constitutionally deficient election process (slate voting, standing vote, failure to record number of voters present).
